title: Proton pump inhibitors and risk of fractures: a meta-analysis of 11 international studies
authors: Yu EW, Bauer SR, Bain PA, Bauer DC
population: 11 observational case-control or cohort studies in 10 publications, mainly in older adults, searched to October 2010
funder: Funding sources: Dr. Bauer is supported by NIH grant K24 AR051895 (National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases).
authorConflicts: None of the authors report any conflicts of interest.
result: PPI use: hip fracture RR 1.30 (95% CI 1.19 to 1.43), spine fracture RR 1.56 (1.31 to 1.85), any-site fracture RR 1.16 (1.04 to 1.30), similar in men and women and by duration. H2-receptor antagonist use was not significantly associated with hip fracture (RR 1.12, 0.97 to 1.30). All studies were observational; residual confounding cannot be excluded.
